## Paid tiers follow the Fairwind release

On 10 November 2026 Google moved Gemini 4 Carbon past the Fairwind Program, where the company says only cybersecurity defenders had it for the two weeks before. The post, by Koray Kavukcuoglu, calls Carbon Google's strongest model, aimed at long runs of knowledge work, software engineering and scientific reasoning. Argon stays the recommended default for most of that work. Carbon is specified for the limit cases, multi-step coding and debugging and open-ended research, and Google says it spends more tokens than Argon on exploration, reasoning and verification loops.

The gate is the paid Gemini API in Google AI Studio and Gemini for business, plus a rollout to Google AI Ultra in the Gemini app, AI Mode in Search and Antigravity. The Verge says it is not clear when, or whether, lower tiers and free users will get Carbon. 9to5Google's reading of the Gemini app picker is that Argon is "Code & analysis" from Google AI Pro up, and Carbon is "Most complex work". The introductory API price matches Argon at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. After 30 November 2026 it rises to $4 and $20.

## Clean contexts meet on a public board

The /swarm command, still a preview, makes the current Antigravity conversation the coordinator. It partitions the task into units that do not collide, typically one worker per file or package, and names them, such as @parser, @api-tests, @docs, or a numbered pool such as @fix-1 through @fix-4. Each worker opens with an empty conversation and a public brief on the shared board: ownership, a list of what not to touch, and a definition of done.

Communication stays on that board, through @mentions, with no private channel. Idle members sleep without spending tokens and wake when mentioned. Usual staffing is one @verifier for every two to four workers. The verifier reads the changes, runs the tests and returns failures to the worker that wrote them. A @monitor posts only if the swarm goes quiet before the work is finished. The coordinator assigns, judges and reports. It does not implement the task.

Google's suggested split puts Carbon on architecture, coordination and auditing, with faster models in parallel isolated copies of the project and verifiers that try to break each change. The docs default every worker to the conversation's model, and you can name another picker model in the prompt. Separate working copies exist for cases where workers would otherwise edit one tree. /swarm is on Google AI Pro and Ultra, in the app and the CLI, which is a wider gate than Carbon itself.

Both showcases Google published start from one prompt. Seven public city-council PDFs and 206 drawing views became a 906K-triangle Three.js model of the Platform 37 office across 10 overnight loops. Historical photos and engineering plates became an interactive 3D exhibition of the Eiffel Tower's construction in 1887 and 1889.

## Vendor benchmarks and a faster quota burn

Google's claims on 10 November 2026 are first place on CursorBench 4.0, Perplexity's WANDR and Zapier's AutomationBench, at more than 2x lower cost per task than the next-best external model, and second place on the Multimodal Knowledge Agent benchmark built with Artificial Analysis, at more than 6x lower average cost per task than the leading model. Google frames that benchmark as work over dense files with charts, images and tables, and says legal, finance and operations output follows strict formatting rules into spreadsheets, presentations and reports.

The Verge points out that companies can and do cherry-pick launch benchmarks. VentureBeat reports that Fable 5.2, released on 9 November, has taken the lead on Artificial Analysis's general intelligence index, where Carbon debuted first. TestingCatalog's trial of an early swarm build took some time and warned of heavy quota use.

Quota scales with workers because each one is an agent. A member that runs out pauses, and does not resume on its own when the quota refreshes. The command is still a preview, and the extra tokens versus Argon are by design.

## Split the work, then read the verifier

On Ultra, run the same limit-case task on Argon and on Carbon, and keep the output you would actually hand on. On Antigravity Pro or Ultra, give /swarm a task whose files or questions do not overlap, name the check, and read the board: briefs, the lines about what not to touch, and the verifier's reports. The number to watch is the quota.

Leave single-file edits and everyday work on the default model. Carbon is not in the free tier in this rollout, and a swarm is the wrong tool when the edits would collide.

Der Befehl /swarm, noch eine Vorschau, macht das laufende Antigravity-Gespräch zur Koordination. Der Auftrag nennt die Zuständigkeit, was nicht angefasst werden darf, und woran fertig zu erkennen ist.

Die Kommunikation bleibt auf diesem Board, über @-Erwähnungen, ohne privaten Kanal. Untätige Mitglieder schlafen, verbrauchen keine Tokens und wachen auf, wenn sie erwähnt werden. Üblich ist ein @verifier auf zwei bis vier Worker. Er liest die Änderungen, führt die Tests aus und gibt Fehler an den Worker zurück, der geschrieben hat. Google schlägt vor, Carbon auf Architektur, Koordination und Prüfung zu setzen, schnellere Modelle in parallelen, getrennten Arbeitskopien laufen zu lassen und jede Änderung von einem Verifier prüfen zu lassen. Googles Angaben vom 10. November 2026: Platz eins auf CursorBench 4.0, auf Perplexitys WANDR und auf Zapiers AutomationBench, bei mehr als 2x niedrigeren Kosten pro Aufgabe als das nächstbeste externe Modell, und Platz zwei auf dem Benchmark Multimodal Knowledge Agent, gebaut mit Artificial Analysis, bei mehr als 6x niedrigeren durchschnittlichen Kosten pro Aufgabe als das führende Modell. Google beschreibt diesen Benchmark als Arbeit über dichte Dateien mit Diagrammen, Bildern und Tabellen und sagt, Ergebnisse für Recht, Finanzen und Betrieb folgten strengen Formatvorgaben in Tabellen, Präsentationen und Berichte.

November, die Spitze im General Intelligence Index von Artificial Analysis übernommen, auf dem Carbon zum Start vorn lag. ## Teile die Arbeit und lies den Verifier

Mit Ultra lässt du dieselbe Grenzaufgabe auf Argon und auf Carbon laufen und behältst das Ergebnis, das du weitergeben würdest. Im Blick behältst du dabei vor allem das Kontingent.

Änderungen an einer einzelnen Datei und die Alltagsarbeit bleiben beim voreingestellten Modell. Carbon liegt in diesem Start nicht im Gratiszugang, und ein Swarm ist das falsche Werkzeug, wenn die Änderungen kollidieren würden.
